label: early copy steps (outputting original tokens 1-2) in long sequences
explanation: Reset-gate unit active almost only in the copy phase (98% of mass), concentrated on the first two steps after the delimiter step, i.e. inputs orig(0) and orig(1) while the model outputs original tokens 1 and 2 (recall_idx 1: 63% of mass, recall_idx 2: 29%). Rate and magnitude grow with sequence length: never active for L<=4, rare at L=5-6, and 57% of mass comes from L=9. Within these steps the input token sets the magnitude: u, v, e, d have the highest rates, and the top activations are on a u copied right after <DEL>. It is weaker on the <DEL> step itself (2% of mass), with a small tail on late copy steps of L=9 sequences. It never fires during the original-input phase. The positional predicate captures 90% of mass, but precision is only about 0.5 because many qualifying steps with non-preferred tokens stay below threshold. Adding a token-set condition raises precision but costs too much recall.
